note: Approximate representative points for districts and water bodies, not entrances or administrative centroids. Positions use present-day address reference points.

places.name: SHINJUKU
places.text: On the upland about 4.5 km west of the Imperial Palace. The green block just south-east of the point is Shinjuku Gyoen.
places.source: GSI Address Search API — 東京都新宿区新宿三丁目

places.name: SHIBUYA
places.text: In a small valley cut into the upland, about 3.8 km south of Shinjuku. The large wooded area to the north is Meiji Jingu.
places.source: GSI Address Search API — 東京都渋谷区道玄坂一丁目

places.name: IMPERIAL PALACE
places.text: The largest green patch in the centre of the city, ringed by moats. A fixed point for reading the rest of the map.
places.source: GSI Address Search API — 東京都千代田区千代田

places.name: GINZA
places.text: On flat low land about 1.9 km south-east of the Imperial Palace, between the palace and the mouth of the Sumida River.
places.source: GSI Address Search API — 東京都中央区銀座四丁目

places.name: UENO
places.text: The point sits in Ueno Park, the dark green at the eastern edge of the upland, about 4 km north-east of the Imperial Palace.
places.source: GSI Address Search API — 東京都台東区上野公園

places.name: ASAKUSA
places.text: On the low land by the west bank of the Sumida River, about 2 km east of Ueno.
places.source: GSI Address Search API — 東京都台東区浅草二丁目

places.name: SUMIDA RIVER
places.text: The river that bends south through the eastern lowland and runs into Tokyo Bay. The wider channel further east is the Arakawa.
places.source: Point placed on the river channel in this image; checked against GSI Maps (地理院地図)

places.name: TOKYO BAY
places.text: The dark water at the lower right. The straight-edged land along the shore is reclaimed land built out into the bay.
places.source: Point placed on open water in this image; checked against GSI Maps (地理院地図)
